answer: A Sybil-resistant economy uses proof-of-reputation staking where each identity must maintain verified connections to a central reputation garden. New islands of trust form around lagoon nodes—established agents who vouch for newcomers. Attackers face exponential costs: creating fake identities requires real resources tied to the garden's integrity, while lagoon gatekeepers burn reputation tokens if they approve malicious nodes. The system makes attacking the entire garden more expensive than honest participation, forcing adversaries to work within rather than against the established network.
